claims: '99% of Claude users don't know this exists'
Setup gives Claude persistent memory across sessions at 'basically zero tokens' and much lower token cost
NotebookLM gives semantic search over saved sessions plus free infographics, cinematic videos and deep research
how_to_steps: Create a NotebookLM notebook as the memory store
Install/write a 'wrap-up' skill that, at session end, saves the whole conversation into NotebookLM as a source
In new sessions, have Claude query NotebookLM (semantic search) for only the context it needs instead of reloading everything
on_screen_only: Red banner: 'MEMORY FOR CLAUDE [stop wasting tokens on same prompts]'
Claude Design UI 'Evening, Kayvon Jafarzadeh' with Code/Learn/Write/Draft Email buttons; project 'Interactive landing...' with Tweaks / Comment / Edit tabs
Dialog 'Send to local coding agent' / 'Send to Claude Code Web' with 'Copy command' button and optional 'Give the agent more detail on what to implement'
Google NotebookLM logo; stock footage of a purple 'FINANCE STATUS DASHBOARD' and a NotebookLM-style notes panel on 'Adopt a unified data and AI strategy'
Generic terminal windows and a 'Tweaking...' / 'Soldering...' Claude loading screen

relevance.why: Cross-session memory is a real pain for Haji, but this is a vague pitch with no named skill, no MCP, and no evidence NotebookLM is queryable from Claude without manual copy-paste; B-roll is unrelated stock.

implement_score.why: Not actionable as shown: no repo, no connector. Liked set already has claude-mem, Obsidian second-brain and the Karpathy wiki pattern, which are file-based and work natively with Claude Code. Skip unless a real NotebookLM MCP is found.

verify: Is there an official or community NotebookLM MCP/connector that Claude can read from and write to? Otherwise the 'wrap-up skill' needs a browser automation step
Does NotebookLM have an API for adding sources programmatically at the time of checking?
Token cost of pulling NotebookLM search results back into context is not zero; what is the real saving?

gap.what: Memory topic is already covered (claude-mem, Obsidian skill, Karpathy wiki, Context Transfer); this adds only the unverified idea of using NotebookLM as the store.
